brackets_single.note: FTB had not yet published official 2026 Schedule X/Y at time of research; 2025 schedule used as most recent confirmed.

surtax.unit: extra % on taxable income above threshold, same threshold for all filing statuses
surtax.note: Mental Health Services Tax; brings the effective top marginal rate to 13.3%.

senior_addl_deduction_per_person.note: CA has no additional standard deduction for 65+; instead gives a small nonrefundable Senior Exemption Credit ($153 single, $306 MFJ, 2025) -- see senior_tax_credits below. Not applied to the computed estimate.

social_security.note: 100% exempt from CA income tax regardless of income level.

retirement_income.note: Pension, 401(k)/403(b), and traditional IRA withdrawals are fully taxed as ordinary income -- no exclusion. Early distributions also carry a 2.5% CA penalty on top of the 10% federal penalty.

senior_tax_credits.note: Senior Head of Household Credit: 2% of CA taxable income, capped at $1,860 (2025); available to filers 65+ who qualified for HOH in one of the prior 2 years due to a spouse's death, with income under $98,652. Senior Exemption Credit: $153 single/$306 MFJ nonrefundable credit (2025), in lieu of an extra deduction. Neither is applied to the computed estimate below -- both are narrow-eligibility or immaterial in size.

effective_rate_pct.unit: % of home value/year, statewide avg effective rate

new_buyer_effective_rate_pct.label: New buyer / recent purchase
new_buyer_effective_rate_pct.unit: % of purchase price/year, typical effective rate for a newly-purchased or newly-built home in year 1
new_buyer_effective_rate_pct.note: Under Prop 13, assessed value resets to purchase price at sale, then grows at most 2%/year, so the statewide-average figure above (blended across decades-long owners with deeply suppressed assessed values) understates what a new buyer pays. Typical range is 1.10%-1.30% (1% constitutional base + local voter-approved bonds/parcel taxes); new-construction developments with Mello-Roos CFD special assessments can run 1.4%-1.8%+ on top of that. Not applied to the computed estimate below, which uses the statewide-average figure.

property_tax.relief_programs_note: Property Tax Postponement Program: age 62+/blind/disabled, ≥40% home equity, no reverse mortgage, 2025-26 household income cap $55,181 -- state pays the current year's tax and places a lien, repaid at sale/transfer/death (does not reduce the tax itself, so not applied to the estimate below). Prop 19 also lets 55+/disabled homeowners transfer their existing lower assessed (Prop 13) value to a new home statewide, up to 3 times -- valuable if downsizing, not modeled here.
